name: Suvorexant

lead: Suvorexant (Belsomra) is a prescription insomnia drug approved in 2014 that blocks the brain's wake-promoting orexin signals. Looksmaxxing users discuss it because better sleep is linked to clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face.

It competitively blocks orexin A and B at OX1 and OX2 receptors, reducing arousal rather than broadly depressing the central nervous system through GABA. Randomised trials, including a one-year trial, reported improvements in time to fall asleep and time awake; no studies look at appearance.

paras: It is taken as a tablet at bedtime on prescription for trouble falling or staying asleep. Sleep effects are noticed from the first nights.
Next-day somnolence, headache and dizziness are reported, with rare complex sleep behaviours. It is Schedule IV in the US and interacts with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and alcohol.

angle.text: Suvorexant is an orexin-blocking prescription sleep drug, discussed on the theory that better sleep shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. Trials show improved sleep latency and wake time in insomnia; appearance has not been studied.

lead: Suvorexant is a dual orexin receptor antagonist developed by Merck and sold as Belsomra. The US FDA approved it in August 2014 as the first drug of its class for insomnia characterised by difficulty with sleep onset and/or maintenance [1][2]. It blocks orexin A and B at OX1 and OX2 receptors, reducing wake-promoting signalling rather than acting through GABA as benzodiazepines and Z-drugs do [1][3][2].

The appearance link is through sleep. Skin, eyes, mood, training recovery and appetite are commonly tied to sleep quality in appearance and fitness communities, so a prescription sleep aid is a tool some people use to try to bank more consistent nights. The chain is indirect: more sleep, better recovery and a rested look. A T Nation poster describing a long struggle with sleep says they tried melatonin, antihistamines, Ambien, Sonata and Belsomra without much success before their doctor moved on to other options [4].
It is Schedule IV in the US [1][2]. Randomised trials, including a one-year trial, reported improvements in sleep latency and wake time with next-day somnolence among reported effects [5][6][7].

paras: Suvorexant is indicated for adults with insomnia [1]. The 2017 American Academy of Sleep Medicine guideline and the 2022 Lancet network meta-analysis include it among insomnia medications, with the guideline recommending it for sleep onset and maintenance [8][9]. A 2025 network meta-analysis compared it with the other orexin antagonists daridorexant and lemborexant [10]. Wikipedia reports that, at 15 to 20 mg, it shortens time to fall asleep by up to about 10 minutes and adds roughly 10 to 20 minutes of total sleep, and that a network meta-analysis found it less effective than benzodiazepines and Z-drugs [2].

A 2024 randomised trial reported less postoperative delirium with suvorexant in older adults after hospitalisation [11], and trials have studied it in Alzheimer's disease with insomnia and in people at high risk of delirium [12][13].

Interest in sleep medicines in appearance communities stems from the belief that adequate sleep supports skin, recovery and body composition. No study has tested suvorexant for any appearance outcome. In the one forum thread in which it appears, the poster reports trying it among several prescription and over-the-counter sleep aids without benefit [4].

Orexin A and B are neuropeptides that promote wakefulness. Suvorexant competitively blocks both orexin receptors [1][14], so it reduces arousal rather than broadly depressing the central nervous system [2]. A 2011 paper described its sleep-promoting effects in preclinical work [15], and a 2015 Nature paper described the crystal structure of the human OX2 receptor bound to suvorexant [16].

Suvorexant is taken orally, peaks in about two to three hours and has a half-life of about 12 hours; it is mainly cleared through CYP3A metabolism, which is why strong CYP3A4 inhibitors raise its levels [2]. Registered Phase 1 studies examined its pharmacokinetics in hepatic and renal impairment [17][18][19].

Next-day somnolence, headache and dizziness are common; abnormal dreams and dry mouth are also described, and complex sleep behaviours have been reported rarely [1][2]. Wikipedia lists contraindication in narcolepsy, interactions with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and additive sedation with alcohol, and reports that tolerance, withdrawal and rebound insomnia do not appear to be significant [1][2]. A 2018 case report describes suvorexant-induced delirium [20]. At doses higher than approved, it produced drug-liking effects similar to zolpidem in recreational sedative users [2]. Its Schedule IV status reflects abuse potential [1].

Merck developed suvorexant under the code MK-4305, and a phase 3 programme ran from 2009 [6][2]. The FDA approved Belsomra on 13 August 2014, making it the first orexin receptor antagonist approved for medical use [1][2]. Newer drugs in the class include lemborexant and daridorexant [10].

Belsomra is prescription-only and a US Schedule IV controlled substance [1][2]. In the forum material that mentions it, it appears alongside older sleep aids as an option people tried when other measures did not help [4].

A phase 3 trial in The Lancet Neurology followed insomnia patients at 106 centres for one year, with abrupt discontinuation after [6][5]. A 2012 Neurology randomised trial and two three-month trials in Biological Psychiatry tested it against placebo [6][7]. Reviews of older-adult sleep medicines and of orexin antagonists summarise further results [14][3].

Registered studies examined hepatic and renal impairment and its use in opioid, alcohol, cannabis and cocaine use disorders, post-operative sleep disturbance, delirium and autism-related sleep problems [17][21][22][23][24][13]. A 2023 randomised trial reported that suvorexant acutely decreased tau phosphorylation and amyloid-beta in the human central nervous system [25]. No studies were found on suvorexant for appearance outcomes.

lore.intro: Suvorexant is rarely discussed in appearance forums; where it appears, it is in threads about sleep problems alongside other sleep aids [4].

claims.claim: Prescription sleep aids can fix poor sleep that is holding back recovery
